items.claim: The rejected-alternative field uses an unanchored positional row reference (the phrase "the row before it") instead of a verse-anchored cross-reference, violating the register rule that cross-row references must be verse-anchored.
items.evidence: strongest_rejected_alternative reads "...distinct from the unanswered spirit-direction question that closes the row before it" -- the phrase "the row before it" names no verse; the intended referent (web:Eccl.3.21's spirit-direction question) is never cited by ref anywhere in this row, unlike the row's own boundary_rationale and every other row in this cluster, which anchor neighbor-comparisons to a verse (e.g. P01-018 cites "4:4", P01-021 cites "4:4's...clause").
tier_citations: register rule: cross-row references are verse-anchored (book_strategy Eccl.md section 8 register hygiene)

items.claim: The 4:1-4:3 span is correctly bounded by its own shavti-formula opening and the fresh raiti-restart at 4:4, with monologue_unit correctly applied as the M-parent default.
items.evidence: The row's own byte-tier quotation of oshb:Eccl.4.1's opening (the shavti/veshavti turning-formula) is one of exactly 3 shavti/veshavti sites (4:1, 4:7, 9:11) per the device inventory -- sweep digit verified. 4:4 opens its own fresh raiti-formula and is the sole marker of a materially new topic (labor-envy); hevel is absent from 4:1-3 but present at 4:4, and tachat-hashemesh brackets 4:1 and 4:3 internally rather than bridging into 4:4 -- no undisclosed cross-seam refrain contradicts the row's own back boundary. The paseq at 4:1 is disclosed tier-appropriately (single-witness, count-only) and correctly not used as a driver.

items.claim: 4:4 is correctly isolated as its own monologue_unit row on the formal shift from first-person raiti-narration to the bare third-person gnomic saying that opens 4:5.
items.evidence: oshb:Eccl.4.4 byte-collates to a first-person raiti-observation clause closing with the reut-ruach formula -- one of exactly 7 reut-ruach sites per the device inventory (1:14, 2:11, 2:17, 2:26, 4:4, 4:6, 6:9) -- sweep digit verified; it also carries a hevel-family token. 4:5 carries neither a first-person marker nor hevel nor reut-ruach, a genuine formal break rather than a thin thematic distinction.

items.claim: 4:5's isolation as a single_saying is warranted: it shares no byte-grounded root or construction with 4:6, so the saying_cluster cohesion bar is correctly judged unmet, and the deviation from the M-parent's monologue_unit default is properly disclosed.
items.evidence: oshb:Eccl.4.5 (the folded-hands proverb) and oshb:Eccl.4.6 (the handful/two-handfuls proverb) share no common root at the byte tier: 4:5's hand term is built on the yod-dalet (hand) root, not the same lexeme as 4:6's kaf/hofnayim (palm/handful) root; 4:6 alone carries the tov-opener and reut-ruach refrains, absent from 4:5, reinforcing the formal split the writer draws.

items.claim: 4:6's isolation as a single_saying is warranted by its own tov-opening comparative construction, one of the book's 12 tov-opener verses, formally distinct from the surrounding first-person and third-person material on both sides.
items.evidence: oshb:Eccl.4.6 is verse-initial tov, one of exactly 12 tov-opener verses per the device inventory (4:6, 4:13, 5:4, 6:9, 7:1, 7:2, 7:3, 7:5, 7:8, 7:11, 7:18, 9:18) -- sweep digit verified; its reut-ruach closing formula matches 4:4's occurrence, but the two verses remain formally distinct (first-person raiti clause at 4:4 vs. bare gnomic construction at 4:6), consistent with keeping them in separate rows.

items.claim: 4:7-4:8 is correctly bounded by its own fresh shavti-restart formula (the second of three book-wide) and correctly held apart from 4:1-3 despite the identical opening formula, with the 4:8 K/Q and paseq disclosures properly tier-labeled and non-driving.
items.evidence: oshb:Eccl.4.7 opens with the second of exactly 3 shavti/veshavti sites (4:1, 4:7, 9:11) -- sweep and ordinal verified. MT 4:8's inline ketiv against its pointed qere (eyes/eye number variant) and its paseq are correctly named against the pmarks inventory and explicitly disclosed as non-drivers, consistent with the inline-ketiv hazard discipline.
tier_citations: device inventory: frame_seams.shavti_turns (3 verses, ordinal verified)

items.claim: The strongest_rejected_alternative for the 4:9-4:12 wisdom_poem call engages only monologue_unit as the rival and skips the closer, byte-grounded rival of saying_cluster, whose own construction-run cohesion bar this unit's threefold conditional pattern arguably satisfies more precisely than wisdom_poem does.
items.evidence: 4:10, 4:11, and 4:12 each open their illustrative clause with a Hebrew conditional particle at the byte tier (ki-im at 4:10, gam-im at 4:11, ve-im at 4:12) -- a genuine three-fold construction run of the kind the granularity gate names as the byte-grounded cohesion evidence required to justify saying_cluster, and closer in form to a small proverb-anthology than to wisdom_poem, which elsewhere in this book strategy denotes the sustained prologue poem (1:3-11) and the aging allegory (11:9-12:7). No first-person verb occurs across 4:9-4:12 (byte-verified in all four verses), which correctly rules out monologue_unit, but that same absence does not by itself decide wisdom_poem over saying_cluster, and the row never engages the latter as a rival.
tier_citations: book_strategy Eccl.md section 6 (saying_cluster cohesion bar: construction runs)

items.claim: The strongest_rejected_alternative denies that any first-person or discourse-restart marker separates 4:14 from 4:15-16, but Eccl.4.15 opens with the first-person raiti-observation verb ("I saw") -- the same device this row's own observed_substrate_signals cites and that sibling rows in this cluster treat as a legitimate discourse-restart marker -- so the stated warrant against splitting at 4:14|4:15 is factually inaccurate on the bytes.
items.evidence: oshb:Eccl.4.15 byte-collates to a raiti-observation opening, a site listed in the device inventory's frame_seams.raiti_observations (which this row itself cites in observed_substrate_signals); the identical formula opens fresh observation cycles elsewhere in this cluster (4:4's raiti-formula, which P01-019 treats as marking a genuine seam). The row's claim of "no first-person...marker" at the proposed split point is therefore contradicted by its own cited evidence; a valid defense of keeping 4:13-16 as one row would need to argue why this particular raiti instance does not override the narrative's grammatical dependency on the antecedent succession, not deny that the marker exists.
